title: Sentence Reconstruction
statement:
You are given a text made of one or more sentences. Every sentence ends with a full stop (`.`). A sentence contains only letters and spaces and has at least one word, but the spacing is messy: there may be several spaces between words, spaces before the first word of a sentence, and spaces after the last full stop of the text.

Rebuild the text as follows:

- Split the text into sentences at the full stops and read the words of each sentence, ignoring all extra spaces.
- If a sentence has **fewer than 5 words**, reverse the order of its words. A sentence with 5 or more words keeps its word order.
- Rewrite each sentence so that its first letter is uppercase and every other letter is lowercase, with the words separated by exactly one space.
- Remove the full stops and join all the sentences, in their original order, with a single space into one line.

Print the resulting line.
inputFormat: A single line containing the text. It ends with a full stop (possibly followed by spaces).
outputFormat: Print the rebuilt text on one line.
constraints: The text contains only English letters, spaces and full stops; every sentence has at least one word

examples.input: The   sun is hot.   programming   is very   fun   today.
examples.output: Hot is sun the Programming is very fun today
examples.explanation: The first sentence has 4 words (fewer than 5), so it becomes "hot is sun The", which is rewritten as "Hot is sun the". The second sentence has 5 words and keeps its order: "Programming is very fun today". Joining them with one space gives the answer.

examples.input: Good   MORNING to you. we are going   to   the   park.
examples.output: You to morning good We are going to the park
examples.explanation: The first sentence has 4 words, so it is reversed to "you to MORNING Good" and then normalised to "You to morning good". The second sentence has 6 words, so only its capitalisation changes.

examples.input: a. b c. d e f.
examples.output: A C b F e d
examples.explanation: Each sentence has fewer than 5 words and is reversed: "a", "c b", "f e d". After capitalising the first letter of each sentence and joining them, the result is "A C b F e d".
